body:
WHAT
The Electron app starts, opens its main window, loads the renderer page, and does not crash. Run with `--smoke` (npm run smoke) it exits 0 about five seconds after the renderer finished loading, or exits 1 if the renderer process died.

WHY
Without a boot check a broken renderer script or a missing module in the packaged build goes unnoticed until a user launches it.

WHERE
app/main.js — const SMOKE = process.argv.includes("--smoke"); createWindow() registers webContents.once("did-finish-load") (app.exit(rendererCrashed ? 1 : 0) after 5000 ms when SMOKE) and webContents.on("render-process-gone") (sets rendererCrashed and app.exit(1) when SMOKE, after the Windows sandbox-rescue relaunch check); app.whenReady() → createWindow(); mainWindow.loadFile(renderer/index.html). app/scripts/launch.js passes --smoke through. app/renderer/index.html is the page loaded, with its ordered <script> list of modules.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Launching with --smoke on a clean userData exits with code 0 within ~10 seconds and the log contains a 'landing-shown' sys event.
2. Launching with --smoke while a renderer module is made to throw at load (or index.html references a missing script) exits nonzero (render-process-gone → exit 1, or a console error surfaced in the log).
3. The single-instance lock is skipped under --smoke so a smoke run can start beside a running app (requestSingleInstanceLock is not called).
4. Without --smoke the app stays running after did-finish-load and does not call app.exit.
5. On Windows, a render-process-gone before the first load without --no-sandbox in argv triggers exactly one relaunch with --no-sandbox appended (and the argv keeps --smoke), instead of exit 1.
